Is there a relationship between the change in property crimes and the change in violent crimes from 2019 to 2020?

Null hypothesis: There is no significant relationship between the change in property crimes and the change in violent crimes.

Alt hypothesis: There is a significant relationship between the change in property crimes and the change in violent crimes.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)

```

md_cities <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/main/data/md_cities_crime_2019_2020.csv"

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r }
md_city_rates <- md_cities %>%
  mutate(
    violent_rate_2019 = (violent2019 / pop2019) * 1000,
    property_rate_2019 = (property2019 / pop2019) * 1000,
    violent_rate_2020 = (violent2020 / pop2020) * 1000,
    property_rate_2020 = (property2020 / pop2020) * 1000
  )
```



```{r }
md_city_change <- md_city_rates %>%
  mutate(
    violent_pct_change = ((violent_rate_2020 - violent_rate_2019) / violent_rate_2019) * 100,
    property_pct_change = ((property_rate_2020 - property_rate_2019) / property_rate_2019) * 100
  )

md_city_change %>%
  summarise(
    mean_2020   = mean(violent_rate_2020, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_2020 = median(violent_rate_2020, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_2020    = min(violent_rate_2020, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_2020    = max(violent_rate_2020, na.rm = TRUE))
 
```

```{r }
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(md_city_change, aes(x = violent_pct_change, y = property_pct_change)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "firebrick") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-200, 100 ), ylim = c(-100, 200)) +
  labs(
    title = "Change in Violent vs Property Crime Totals (2019–2020)",
    x = "Change in Property Crimes",
    y = "Change in Violent Crimes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


```

```{r }
cor.test(md_city_change$violent_pct_change, md_city_change$property_pct_change)


```
 
 Though the test shows a significant result (p < 0.05), the graph only shows a small upward trend with many outlies. This means that when property crime goes up, violent crime also goes up a little, but not by much. So, the hypothesis is a little supported, but not completely proven
